references.text: The Nazirite also had special rules regarding impurity from death, but could become unclean for close relatives, showing parallel provisions for holy persons.
Ezekiel describes similar rules for the priests in the future temple, where they could become unclean for close relatives, including an unmarried sister.
The immediate context establishes the rule that priests must not make themselves unclean by contact with a dead body, except for close relatives.
The high priest had stricter rules and could not become unclean even for father or mother, unlike ordinary priests who could become unclean for close relatives.
General laws about impurity from touching dead bodies, which form the basis for the special exceptions given to priests.
